title: Cheat day: do you need one, and how to do it without ruining your progress
intro: You don't need a cheat day to lose weight, but you can enjoy your favourite food without guilt. Usually one planned 'free meal' is safer than a whole day of unlimited eating.

sections.h: Why a whole day can be a problem
sections.p: To lose 0.5 kg a week, you need a deficit of an estimated 3500 kcal a week. One day of unlimited eating at a buffet, bubble tea and dessert can add 1500-2500 kcal extra. Half or more of a week's effort can be lost in one day.
Plan one or two meals a week that you really love. For example nasi kandar with friends or an office birthday cake. Eat relaxed, enjoy it, and go back to your usual routine at the next meal.
Have a high-protein, light breakfast and lunch on that day. Don't arrive at the buffet too hungry. Pick what you love most and skip the 'just okay' stuff.

sections.h: Weight up the next day? Normal
sections.p: Salty food and lots of carbs make your body hold water. The scale may go up 0.5-1.5 kg the next day. That's mostly water, not fat, and it usually goes down in 2-4 days if you go back to your routine.
No need to skip meals or over-exercise the next day. That can trigger a cycle of overeating and guilt. Continue your usual plan, drink enough water and sleep early.

action: Pick one free meal this week and set the day.
On that day, have a breakfast and lunch with protein and vegetables.
Don't weigh yourself for 2 days after a big meal.
After your free meal, go straight back to your usual meals at the next mealtime.
myth: Many believe a cheat day 'shocks' your metabolism so you lose weight faster. Actually, one day of eating a lot has no magic effect; it just adds calories for that week.

faq.q: What if there's a wedding kenduri every week?
faq.a: Treat the kenduri as your free meal. Take a little rice, enough chicken or meat, and vegetables. Enjoy it, then eat light at home.

faq.q: I feel guilty after eating a lot. Is that normal?
faq.a: Many people feel that way. Remember, one meal doesn't ruin your progress. What matters is what you do consistently, week after week.

faq.q: When is the best time for a free meal?
faq.a: Pick a time when there's an event or time with family and friends. That way, you enjoy the food and the moment, not eating alone because of stress.
